title: Pausing the key at selected F runes
reader_title: Can leaving selected F runes unchanged fix keyword decoding?
reader_intro: Tries each choice of F runes to leave unchanged while pausing the key, using one assigned keyword per page, and checks whether every one-rune word becomes I or A.
reader_finding: No choice of F pauses made every one-rune word read I or A on the ten tested pages; shuffled pages failed the same test, so this result does not establish whether F is an interruption.
reader_limit: The result uses ten assigned keys and the program's exact spelling and word-break rules; other keys, corrected spellings or different ways of pausing at F were not tested.
question: Does the pinned second-layer program find any fixed-key F-skip mask that satisfies all its singleton I/A constraints?
reader_question: Can treating selected F runes as literal fix these keyword decodes?
summary: None of 27,402 source-defined F masks across ten exact pages passes all one-rune-word checks; the program falls back to choosing a mask by frequency score.
finding: Exact pinned Wulfic pages 21–30 align to LP2-04–13. The unmodified source enumerates 27,402 literal-F masks, and no page has a mask satisfying all of its singleton I/A constraints. Its 45 fixed second-layer rune routes per page on the unmasked decode also print zero gate-passing rows. Nineteen whole-selection shuffled searches likewise have zero gated pages, so this gate does not distinguish the manuscript from the stated shuffle control.
limitations: The source keyword parser drops V in DIVINITY and contracts EO in DEOR; this replay preserves its actual arrays. The source's narrow singleton separator rule and IoC/bigram score are not a general reading test. The 19 shuffles are a coarse descriptive reference, not a cipher model. Other keys, page ranges, interruption rules or downstream layers are not tested.
next_steps: Specify a corrected key/parser and a held-out passage test before treating an increased IoC from a selected mask as a decoding lead.

scope.representation: Exact source Git-object rune files pages/page_21–30, rune-aligned to current LP2-04–13; the source's word separators and keyword parser.
scope.procedure: For each fixed page keyword/mode, enumerate every subset of ciphertext F positions as literal, non-advancing key slots. Apply the original all-singleton I/A gate, source score or fallback IoC rank, and source-defined unmasked second-layer routes. Run 19 complete page-shuffle controls.
scope.parameters: Ten pages, 1–14 F positions each, 27,402 total source masks, 45 fixed rune routes per page, 19 pagewise shuffle repeats, seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: Corrected keyword parse, alternate F behavior, source pages outside 21–30, word-boundary variants, other languages and uncalled prime permutation helper.

review.kind: complete source-defined F-mask replay and selected-search control
review.reviewer: Ten Git-object/page alignments, two-pause planted recovery, 48 scalar/source parity cases, unmodified source output receipt, independent enumeration of all 27,402 observed masks and one shuffled full grid

reproduction.environment: Python 3, NumPy and Numba. The full run, source parity and input snapshot also require a checkout of pinned Wulfic commit bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c.

visuals.caption: Selected F masks can raise IoC on each page, but none passes the source's all-singleton I/A gate.

browser_followups.motivation: Change the rune numbers using the same three-number pattern for every word, starting the pattern over at each word. Leave F runes unchanged and pause the pattern at those runes. The earlier check carried the pattern across the page; this version lets us inspect what restarting it changes. It does not judge whether the output is a reading.
browser_followups.title: Should each word use the same starting pattern?
browser_followups.question: What does the fixed DEOR rule output when F stays literal and the key restarts at every word?
browser_followups.scope_change: Keep LP2-11 and the source DEOR array [23, 12, 4], subtraction and phase zero. Copy every F unchanged without consuming a key rune, then restart the key at every non-rune boundary. The earlier mask search tested page-local key counters, including the all-F mask; it did not restart at words.
browser_followups.limitation: This is a new descriptive clock variant, not a replay of the source singleton gate, mask selection or IoC/bigram ranking. The browser reports the complete output and basic rune metrics. It does not identify readable language, claim a decryption or test other keys, phases, selective F masks, page joins or cipher layers. Every non-rune ends a transcription word; these are not verified plaintext word boundaries.

value.detail: Report the declared transform and descriptive rune metrics; no plaintext or significance threshold is inferred.

control.label: Recover every independently specified output rune in a synthetic control
